input.command: ls -R | grep -v node_modules | head -30; cat package.json bin/csv2json.js src/parse.js; ls test; head -40 test/*.js; cat README.md

result.builder:
## Criteria the build must meet (word for word)
1. `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]` followed by a newline and exits 0.
2. With --tsv, commas inside a field stay literal: `printf 'name\tnote\nx\thello, world\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"name":"x","note":"hello, world"}]` followed by a newline.
3. With --tsv and several data rows, every row comes out in order: `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n3\t4\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"},{"a":"3","b":"4"}]` followed by a newline.
4. Without the flag, CSV still works as before: `printf 'a,b\n1,2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]` followed by a newline.
5. Without the flag, tabs are not treated as separators: `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js` prints exactly `[{"a\tb":"1\t2"}]` followed by a newline, which is the current output.
6. `npm test` exits 0, and test/ contains at least one test that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on tab-separated input and checks its output.
7. README.md documents the --tsv flag with an example invocation.

## Limits (non-goals)
- Quoted fields, escaped separators, or any RFC 4180 or full TSV quoting rules. Fields are split naively, as they are today.
- Auto-detecting the separator, or adding a general --sep/--delimiter option.
- Changing what happens with unknown command-line arguments, or adding --help.
- Changing JSON output formatting or how the header row is used.

## Steps
1. Read bin/csv2json.js, src/parse.js, test/csv.test.js and README.md. parse(text, sep = ',') in src/parse.js already takes a separator; the CLI currently ignores argv and always calls parse(text).
2. In bin/csv2json.js, check whether `--tsv` appears anywhere in `process.argv.slice(2)`. If it does, call parse(text, '\t'); otherwise call parse(text) exactly as today. Keep input from stdin only and keep the output format (`JSON.stringify(...)` plus a trailing newline) unchanged. Do not add handling for other arguments. Leave src/parse.js unchanged unless you find a real need.
3. In test/csv.test.js (keep the existing node --test setup and existing tests), add tests that run `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` via execFileSync with tab-separated input and assert the exact stdout, covering: the basic case `a\tb\n1\t2\n` -> `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]\n`; a field containing a comma (`name\tnote\nx\thello, world\n`); multiple data rows in order. Also add a test that without the flag, tab input gives `[{"a\\tb":"1\\t2"}]\n` (the current behaviour).
4. In README.md, add a short section documenting `--tsv`: say it reads tab-separated input instead of CSV, with an example such as `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv`. Keep the existing CSV usage.
5. From the repo root, run each command from criteria 1-5 yourself and compare output byte for byte, then run `npm test` and confirm it exits 0.
6. Open one pull request with these changes.
result.verifier:
Work at the PR head, from the repository root. Run every command; do not judge from the diff alone. Compare outputs byte for byte (e.g. pipe into `od -c` or compare with `diff` against the expected string) so a trailing newline and exact characters are checked.

## Check 1 — expect: `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]` followed by a newline and exits 0.
Run: `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv > /tmp/o1; echo "exit=$?"; printf '%s\n' '[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]' | cmp - /tmp/o1 && echo SAME`
PASS: exit=0 and SAME (stdout is exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]` plus one newline).
FAIL: any other exit code, or any difference in stdout.

## Check 2 — expect: With --tsv, commas inside a field stay literal: `printf 'name\tnote\nx\thello, world\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"name":"x","note":"hello, world"}]` followed by a newline.
Run: `printf 'name\tnote\nx\thello, world\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv | cmp - <(printf '%s\n' '[{"name":"x","note":"hello, world"}]') && echo SAME`
PASS: SAME printed.
FAIL: cmp reports a difference, or the command errors.

## Check 3 — expect: With --tsv and several data rows, every row comes out in order: `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n3\t4\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"},{"a":"3","b":"4"}]` followed by a newline.
Run: `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n3\t4\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv | cmp - <(printf '%s\n' '[{"a":"1","b":"2"},{"a":"3","b":"4"}]') && echo SAME`
PASS: SAME printed.
FAIL: any difference (missing row, wrong order, extra output) or an error.

## Check 4 — expect: Without the flag, CSV still works as before: `printf 'a,b\n1,2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]` followed by a newline.
Run: `printf 'a,b\n1,2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js | cmp - <(printf '%s\n' '[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]') && echo SAME`
PASS: SAME printed.
FAIL: any difference or an error.

## Check 5 — expect: Without the flag, tabs are not treated as separators: `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js` prints exactly `[{"a\tb":"1\t2"}]` followed by a newline, which is the current output.
Run: `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js | cmp - <(printf '%s\n' '[{"a\tb":"1\t2"}]') && echo SAME` (here `\t` must be the two literal characters backslash and t, i.e. the JSON escape; the single-quoted `'%s\n'` argument keeps them literal).
PASS: SAME printed — output is the JSON array with one key `a\tb` (JSON tab escape) and value `1\t2`, plus one newline.
FAIL: any difference, e.g. the output splits into keys a and b.

## Check 6 — expect: `npm test` exits 0, and test/ contains at least one test that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on tab-separated input and checks its output.
Run: `npm test; echo "exit=$?"`, then `grep -n -- '--tsv' test/*.js` and read each matching test.
PASS: exit=0, and at least one test in test/ executes bin/csv2json.js with the `--tsv` argument, feeds it input containing tab characters, and asserts on its output.
FAIL: npm test exits non-zero, or no test in test/ runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on tab-containing input and asserts on the output (e.g. only parse() is tested directly, or the output is not checked).

## Check 7 — expect: README.md documents the --tsv flag with an example invocation.
Run: `grep -n -- '--tsv' README.md` and read README.md.
PASS: README.md mentions the --tsv flag, explains it is for tab-separated input, and shows an example invocation using it (such as `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv`).
FAIL: no mention of --tsv, or no example invocation that uses it.

## Advisory
- Not part of PASS/FAIL: check the flag also works when not first among arguments (e.g. `node bin/csv2json.js foo --tsv`), and that src/parse.js behaviour for existing callers is unchanged.
- Note any scope creep against the issue's non-goals (a general --sep option, --help, quoting rules, changed output formatting) as a remark only.

text:
I wrote both briefs for issue #5 (the `--tsv` flag), and the harness accepted them, so they're now fixed. I didn't change any code.

**Builder brief:**
- It opens with the seven expect lines word for word, then the four non-goals as limits.
- The suggested approach: in `bin/csv2json.js`, look for `--tsv` anywhere in the arguments. If it's there, call the existing `parse(text, '\t')`; otherwise call `parse(text)` as today. `src/parse.js` stays as it is.
- It asks for new tests in `test/csv.test.js` that run `bin/csv2json.js --tsv` on: the basic case, a field containing a comma, and several rows. It also asks for one test showing that tab input without the flag still gives today's output.
- It asks for a README section with an example such as `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv`.
- Before opening the pull request, the builder runs each expect command and `npm test` itself.

**Verifier brief:**
- It has one check per expect line, in the same order.
- Checks 1–5 run the exact command and compare the output byte for byte against the expected string with `cmp`, so the trailing newline is checked too. Check 1 also requires exit code 0.
- Check 6 runs `npm test`. It then searches `test/` for `--tsv` and reads the matching test to confirm it runs the program on tab-containing input and checks the output.
- Check 7 reads `README.md` for the flag, what it means, and an example invocation.
- Under an "Advisory" heading, outside PASS/FAIL: whether the flag works when it isn't the first argument, and any work beyond the non-goals.

**One fix to the issue's own proof:** the proof for the `npm test` line said to run `npm run test:cli`, but `package.json` has no such script, so following it would fail. The verifier runs `npm test` instead, which is what the expect line actually says.
